abstract: Causal set theory postulates discrete spacetime events endowed with a partial order, while measurement theory postulates irreducible events associated with collapse or irreversibility. We show that both structures arise as the same four-dimensional shadow of coherence-selection events in Modal Triplet Theory (MTT). Selection events are defined as irreversible basin transitions under noninvertible projection of the coherent sector. We prove that these events generate a locally finite partial order, yielding an effective causal set whose density, ordering, and approximate Lorentz invariance are fixed by coherent-sector bottleneck data rather than by ad hoc sprinkling assumptions. Deviations from Poisson statistics and exact Lorentz invariance are predicted near coherence-breakdown regions. We relate these results to ongoing work in causal set theory, continuous measurement, and collapse physics, and establish cross-sector closure: the same bottleneck vector controls event density, collapse thresholds, ultraviolet completion, and canonical geometric discreteness. All statements are slab-local and admissibility-conditioned.
